data.title: US judge declines long-term ban on Trump admin's taxpayer-funded ads
data.description:
A federal judge has declined to issue a long-term ban on the Trump administration's controversial taxpayer-funded political advertisements, leaving their future in the hands of a different judge who is overseeing a similar case.

US District Judge Jennifer L Rochon in New York argued on Friday that the suing coalition, which includes the government watchdog group Common Cause, didn't convincingly prove the ads were still causing them "imminent and irreparable harm" now that November's midterm elections are over.

"The urgency of the earlier requests for temporary injunctive relief in this case centered around the November 3, 2026, midterm and state elections," Rochon wrote in a court filing. "Those elections have now passed." The incremental victory for the Trump administration comes as a parallel case unfolds in Washington, DC.

 

In that case, the Democratic National Committee has asked the court for a preliminary injunction to stop the Trump administration from developing, distributing or airing the ads. The judge hasn't yet ruled on that matter after a hearing earlier this week.

At issue in Friday's ruling were TV spots the Trump administration started airing in September that were paid for at least in part by a USD 20 million Department of Homeland Security contract.

Some of the ads glorified the president with highlight reels of scenic speeches and callouts about tax cuts and support for law enforcement. One of them repurposed a clip that had been used by Trump's 2024 presidential campaign, showing him walking down a hallway as his voice can be heard warning of a "final battle" against "globalists" and "warmongers." Some of the ads also appeared on Trump administration social media channels and the White House website.

The plaintiffs had argued the ads were illegal government-sponsored propaganda intended to promote the president's campaign message just weeks before Election Day. The White House has defended the ads as public service announcements.

The judges in both cases issued temporary restraining orders blocking some of the ads in the lead-up to the election. A temporary restraining order in the Democrats' case expires next week.

Bradley Girard, senior counsel at Democracy Forward, which represented the plaintiffs in the New York case, said while the team is disappointed, "we will continue to pursue this case on the merits to prevent this from happening in the future." The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

data.title: Only 4 of 10 richest Indians rank among country's top philanthropists
data.description:
India’s wealthy gave 11 per cent more to philanthropy in 2025-26 (FY26), with the number of philanthropists on the EdelGive Hurun India Philanthropy List reaching a record 219, up from 192 a year earlier, but only four of the 10 richest Indians on the M3M Hurun India Rich List 2026 — Shiv Nadar & family, Gautam Adani & family, Mukesh Ambani & family and the Poonawallas (Cyrus and Adar) — also featured among the top 10 philanthropists.
 
The remaining six positions were occupied by donors who did not make the country’s top 10 richest list. These included the Bajaj family, Nandan Nilekani, Kumar Mangalam Birla, Sudhir and Samir Mehta, Ranjan Pai and Rohini Nilekani (who does not feature on the Rich List at all).
 
 
The top 10 philanthropists gave ₹6,572 crore, or almost 57 per cent of the total.  Together, the 219 Indians donated ₹11,554 crore between April 1, 2025 and March 31, 2026, an 11 per cent increase from ₹10,380 crore in FY25.
 
The list covers  Indians who gave at least ₹5 crore. It includes only those willing to disclose their giving, so the actual number of philanthropists and the total donated could be higher. A donor’s total includes personal giving as well as donations made by companies they own, in proportion to their shareholding. 
 
Personal giving still under half
 
Out of the 192, only 42 donors donated from their personal wealth, contributing ₹5,413 crore, making 47 per cent of the total. 53 per cent still came through company Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives. Only six of the top 10 philanthropists gave majorly from personal wealth, while the other four — Adani, Bajaj, Ambani and Birla — based their giving mostly on CSR.
 
Nadar leads, Adani surges
 
Shiv Nadar and family retained the top spot for the fifth year, giving ₹2,593 crore, or ₹7.1 crore a day. This was 4 per cent lower than last year, and 93 per cent of it was personal. Arts, culture and heritage took the largest share at ₹1,220 crore.
 
Gautam Adani and family moved up three places to second, with giving up 127 per cent to ₹877 crore from ₹386 crore. The ₹491 crore rise is the largest on the list. The Bajaj family stayed third at ₹632 crore, and Mukesh Ambani and family were fourth at ₹620 crore.
 
Nandan Nilekani rose to fifth with ₹380 crore, almost all of it personal. He has also donated 10.1 per cent of his wealth since 2019, the highest percentage among anyone in the top 10. Kumar Mangalam Birla and family were sixth at ₹366 crore, with 16 per cent of it coming from personal funds. Cyrus S Poonawalla and Adar Poonawalla (₹336 crore) and Sudhir Mehta and Samir Mehta (₹334 crore) followed. Ranjan Pai and family entered the top 10 philanthropists list at ninth with ₹219 crore, of which 98 per cent came from personal funds.
 
Women philanthropists increase their presence
 
Twenty-nine women feature in the list this year, up from 24 last year. Rohini Nilekani, who ranks tenth with ₹215 crore, is the most generous woman on the list, ahead of Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw (₹93 crore) and Anu Aga and family (₹78 crore). Rohini Nilekani is the only person on the overall list to have donated almost a 100 per cent in a personal capacity, and has donated ₹1,121 crore since 2019.
 
The 19 donors who gave ₹100 crore each or more, just 9 per cent of the list, accounted for ₹7,838 crore, or 68 per cent of all donations. At the other end, 80 donors who gave ₹5-10 crore each make up 37 per cent of the list but only 5 per cent of the giving.
 
New donors, new causes
 
There were 45 new entrants, up from 12 last year, and they contributed ₹696 crore. Raamdeo Agrawal (₹120 crore) and Motilal Oswal (₹119 crore) led them, followed by Chandrika and Ranjan Tandon (₹100 crore), whose gift will set up a School of Artificial Intelligence at IIM Ahmedabad.
 
Self-made donors number 125, or 57 per cent of the list, and account for 65 per cent of the total donations. Education remained the top cause at ₹4,188 crore (share of 36 per cent). Healthcare rose 82 per cent to ₹1,768 crore, and environment and sustainability rose 86 per cent to ₹813 crore. Social development and Skill development saw the fastest growth, at 1,466 per cent and 1,614 per cent respectively.
 
Mumbai has the most philanthropists at 64, but New Delhi leads by value with ₹3,168 crore.
 
The biggest movers
 
The sharpest jump in rank belongs to Farukbhai Gulambhai Patel of KP Group, who climbed 105 places to 48th by giving ₹30 crore, up from ₹7 crore a year earlier. The largest percentage increase was recorded by Irfan Razack, Noaman Razack and Rezwan Razack of Prestige Estates Projects, whose giving rose 425 per cent to ₹42 crore.
 
CSR: Record unspent funds
 
Among BSE 200 companies, CSR spending was ₹18,922 crore, close to last year’s record of ₹18,963 crore. But unspent CSR hit a record ₹2,290 crore, up from ₹1,920 crore, while spending above the mandate fell to ₹1,107 crore from ₹1,821 crore. The net shortfall of ₹1,183 crore is the widest in over a decade. Reliance Industries spent ₹1,223 crore against a mandated ₹1,032 crore.
 
Anas Rahman Junaid, founder of Hurun India, said India’s earlier stage of wealth creation suggests room to grow. China’s list has 30 donors giving at least $15 million each, against 19 in India giving ₹100 crore or more. “As our economy doubles, our ambition should be to more than double the number of large philanthropists,” he said.

data.title: Doing our bit: India Inc responds to PM's wake-up call on jobs and pay
data.description:
A day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi came down heavily on India Inc for not creating jobs and hiking salaries despite steep corporate tax cuts, Vedanta group Chairman Anil Agarwal said the company had just recently “introduced a special ‘Chairman Grant’, providing nearly 100,000 employees with an additional 10 per cent of their annual salary”.
 
Other industry leaders and business associations said they, too, were doing their bit, with some also making a case for additional measures to boost employment in their respective sectors. There was, however, no immediate reaction from major industry bodies.
 
Modi, in his address on Thursday at the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry’s annual general meet, had pulled up corporate India for its continued dependence on imports in sectors such as pharmaceuticals and metals, and for treating the country’s vast domestic market as a “comfort zone” rather than raising product quality and building capabilities to compete globally.
  
Mohini Milind Kelkar, president, Indian Machine Tool Manufacturers’ Association (IMTMA), said the association shared the Prime Minister’s concerns and had been working to bridge the workforce shortage.
 
While acknowledging the mining sector’s “significant potential to generate employment, both directly and through allied activities such as transportation, equipment manufacturing and downstream processing”, the Federation of Indian Mineral Industries said that encouraging investment in mining and value addition, along with skill development, would help create quality employment. This would “strengthen India’s mineral security and reduce dependence on imports”, its spokesperson said.
 
Expressing the industry’s support to the PM’s call, Sanjay Mehta, president, Material Recycling Association of India, added, “However, the material recycling sector has a unique challenge. India’s domestic scrap generation is currently insufficient to meet the growing requirements of its recycling industries, which is a key raw material.” Consequently, Mehta said, imports of quality scrap become “inevitable”.
 
Echoing the sentiment, Rajamani Krishnamurti, president, Indian Stainless Steel Development Association (ISSDA), said the Prime Minister’s remarks resonated strongly with the Indian stainless steel industry’s aspirations and ground realities — but certain structural challenges needed urgent attention if India is to realise its full manufacturing potential. The ISSDA would like to highlight the need for strengthening raw material security, immediate implementation of quality control orders, fair trade and not unfair competition.
 
Krishnamurti pointed to priority issues such as addressing unfair trade practices, promoting domestic value addition and encouraging investment, technology and employment. The central message of the Indian stainless steel industry, he added, was that it does not seek protection from competition; it seeks a level playing field.
 
Ajai Rana of the Federation of Seed Industry of India (FSII) said India’s seed industry is recruiting people, and though the industry is sitting on huge inventories, it has not retrenched anyone.
 
Most industry players were largely supportive of the Prime Minister’s call. Some also listed the factors holding them back.
 
“The biggest drawbacks are bureaucracy and a parallel economy, both of which are hurting the country,” said a senior industry player who did not wish to be named. Another India Inc representative, who spoke on anonymity, added that the question of creating jobs and passing on the tax benefits varied from sector to sector. “Some industries, such as kitchenware and appliances, are adding jobs since they are growing,” the official said. That said, there has been a lull in major manufacturing sectors, the official added.
 
A representative from the roads and infrastructure sector said the issues facing the roads sector were rather complicated with matters such as premium, bonus etc dominating the discourse.
 
The Vedanta Group, meanwhile, said in a note that the group had also built a democratised employee stock option (ESOP) programme, extending ownership opportunities from entry-level professionals, including freshers, to senior leadership, covering nearly 40 per cent of its workforce.
 
A senior NITI Aayog official urged the industry to view the government as a facilitator, not just as an entity for financial sops.

data.title: MCA proposes NFRA recruitment changes, deputation tenure may rise to 7 yrs
data.description:
The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) has proposed changes to the recruitment and service rules of the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA), including extending the maximum deputation period for its officers from five to seven years and revising experience requirements for senior positions.
 
Under the proposed amendments to the NFRA (Recruitment, Salary, Allowances and Other Terms and Conditions of Service of Secretary, Officers and Other Employees of Authority) Rules, 2019, officers appointed on deputation could have their tenure extended by two years at a time, subject to a maximum period of seven years. The existing rules allow a maximum deputation period of five years.
 
 
NFRA, established under the Companies Act, 2013, is responsible for monitoring compliance with accounting and auditing standards. It fills positions through different routes, including direct recruitment, promotion of existing employees and deputation or short-term contractual appointments.
 
In a submission to Parliament's Standing Committee on Finance earlier this year, MCA said 34 of the 53 sanctioned posts in NFRA, excluding support staff, were filled, leaving 19 vacant. The proposed longer tenure could help NFRA retain deputationists for extended periods.
 
Notably, the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, seeks to expand the regulator's powers, enabling it to issue advisories, censures or warnings, among other things.
 
The draft also proposes changing how manager posts are filled. The share for direct recruitment would fall from 40 per cent to 15 per cent, while the share for promotion of existing employees would rise from 30 per cent to 55 per cent. Promotion posts that cannot be filled for lack of eligible candidates would go to deputation, instead of direct recruitment as at present. The remaining 30 per cent would continue to be filled through deputation or short-term contracts.
 
The proposed shift towards internal promotion for manager posts comes around the time when the first batch of officers hired directly, at the assistant manager and manager levels, became eligible for promotion starting 1 January 2026, according to another earlier submission by MCA to the committee.
 
For assistant general manager appointments, the draft proposes reducing the required regular service for eligible Central and All India Civil Services officers at Pay Level 10 from seven years to four years. It also removes the existing three-year minimum service requirement for officers appointed regularly at Level 11.
 
However, for senior positions like chief general manager, general manager and deputy general manager, the draft proposes to increase minimum experience requirements for officers from the Reserve Bank of India, banks, financial institutions, regulatory bodies and other specified institutions.

data.title: PM 'rattled', realised he will be 'outgoing PM' soon, says Congress
data.description:
The Congress on Friday claimed that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s “verbal assault” on wealth creators showed that he had realised he would soon become the “outgoing PM”. The party said he was blaming others when he should be looking within at his own policies, which were responsible for the economic situation.
 
The opposition party said that instead of questioning others, the Prime Minister should acknowledge the shortcomings in his government’s performance and the “failure” of its policies.
 
Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh said Modi must admit that after 12 years, “inflation remains uncontrolled, sufficient employment opportunities are not being created, and the pace of private investment is sluggish”.
 
 
“Mr Prime Minister, the economy cannot be run merely by delivering speeches or offering advice to industrialists. It requires sound policies, an environment of trust, and an accountable government. The nation’s industrial sector deserves far better treatment and policies,” Ramesh said at a press conference.
 
“Yesterday, the PM addressed industry leaders at a Ficci event. The way he addressed the gathering, it was clear that he was rattled, frustrated, dejected, concerned and disappointed. He attacked the same wealth creators. He repeated what we had said in our manifesto,” he said.
 
Meanwhile, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday also attacked the Prime Minister over his remarks on job creation and wage growth. He said the PM’s criticism of industrialists amounted to an admission of his own government’s role in creating monopolies and undermining a level playing field.
 
Reacting on X, Rahul Gandhi alleged that airports, ports, mines, forests, electricity, coal and roads had been handed over to a select few, and questioned how many jobs they had created.

data.title: Urban funding, affordable housing top agenda ahead of FY28 Budget
data.description:
Experts from the housing, urbanisation and culture sectors on Friday suggested developing greater absorptive capacity for funds for urban local governments/bodies (ULBs/ULGs), rejuvenating urban infrastructure sustainably in heritage zones, and rental housing interventions during the ninth pre-Budget consultation with Union Finance and Corporate Affairs Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, sources said.
 
Sitharaman chaired the consultation in the national capital as part of preparations for the Union Budget 2027-28. The meeting was also attended by the secretaries of the Department of Economic Affairs and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA).
 
According to the sources, discussions on housing focused on greater emphasis on Transit-Oriented Development (TOD), rental housing and affordable housing. TOD is an urban planning approach that concentrates dense, mixed-use neighbourhoods around high-capacity public transport hubs.
 
With cities being poised as the future growth hubs in the run up to 2047, several states have begun reworking their city master plans for better planning of urban agglomerations, managing unchecked and unplanned urbanisation, and developing cities around key transport modes like metro and buses. Earlier this year, the Delhi government released its Delhi Master Plan 2047, which eyes building of four million new homes, and proposes land pooling (with a reduced 20-hectare threshold) and TOD along metro/transit corridors to unlock large-scale housing.
 
Some stakeholders also suggested ensuring absorptive capacity for ULBs and ULGs. The concern here is that states are likely to receive funds both from the Urban Challenge Fund (UCF) and devolution from finance comission, and cities need enough absorptive capacity for these funds, a source said.
 
The Rs 1-trillion UCF, which was announced in the 2025-26 Budget, shifts urban funding from pure grants towards market-linked, reform-driven and outcome-based projects. The eligibility for the scheme would require states to make urban projects bankable, and a lot of the work on this requires organisation of municipal accounts, credit ratings, and having clear market-driven revenue models.
 
In this regard, stakeholders also sought a framework to reward cities for their performance in initiating urban reforms. While larger cities could undertake work under the UCF more easily, smaller cities might struggle, a source said.
 
On heritage and development, one source said work in historic city areas did not fall under any single ministry. Instead, it fell between the urban development and culture ministries, creating policy gaps. Another proposal was to rejuvenate inner-city village areas in a sustainable manner.
 
Experts at the meeting included Shekhar Patel, national president of the Confederation of Real Estate Developers' Associations of India (Credai); Srikanth Viswanathan, chief executive officer at Janaagraha; Vipul Roongta, managing director and chief executive officer of HDFC Capital Advisors; and Samir Jasuja, founder and managing director of PropEquity, among others.

data.title: Anthropic's IPO attracts $120 billion in retail demand, surpassing SpaceX
data.description:
By Anthony Hughes
 
Anthropic PBC’s initial public offering drew roughly between $115 billion and $120 billion of demand for shares from retail investors, according to a person familiar with the matter, more than the amount sought by them in SpaceX’s debut.  
The frontier AI lab’s first-time share sale had well over $500 billion of demand from institutional investors, more than double the orders for shares in SpaceX, the person said, asking not to be identified as the information isn’t public.
 
Anthropic’s IPO is the biggest of all time, with the $93.5 billion raised by the company and its seven co-founders, including the over-allotment, comfortably topping SpaceX’s $86.2 billion offering. Anthropic also raised $26 billion in a private placement, for a total haul of $119.5 billion. 
Even as the IPO delivered a record amount to the company, adding to the nearly $132 billion of cash and equivalents it had as of Sept. 30, Anthropic’s shares erased much of their first-day jump on Friday, testing investors’ faith after the AI lab delivered the biggest initial public offering in history.
 
 
Shares of Anthropic fell as much as nearly 15 per cent on Friday, after the stock gained 17 per cent in its first trading day as a public company. The trading gives Anthropic a market value of about $1.5 trillion, ranking it among the 15 biggest publicly traded companies in the world.
 
Most of the stock in Anthropic’s IPO went to long-only investors and sovereign wealth funds, with venture capital investors receiving a low-to-mid single digit percentage point share in aggregate, the person said. Banks working on the first-time share sale, led by Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Morgan Stanley, allocated fewer shares to investors relative to the size of the offering than those who placed orders for SpaceX’s IPO, they said.
 
Retail investors in Anthropic’s IPO received about 15 per cent of the shares available, Bloomberg News reported. 
 
Some of the details of the demand were previously reported by the International Financial Review and the Financial Times. Representatives for Anthropic, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley declined to comment.
 
SpaceX’s IPO maintained its dominance in some corners of the retail universe. Demand for Anthropic’s IPO was second to SpaceX’s first-time share sale, still the record-holder on both Robinhood Markets Inc. and Charles Schwab Corp.’s platforms. 
 
More than 360,000 people requested shares in the Anthropic IPO through Robinhood Financial and Trade PMR, and everyone who requested a share received at least one, if not more, a Robinhood spokesperson said. AI-related shares led activity on Schwab’s platform on Friday, with Anthropic among the top five names, according to a Schwab spokesperson.
 
Anthropic’s IPO left more than half of the institutional investors bidding for stock without any shares, with allocations heavily skewed toward US-based investors, Bloomberg News reported. About 1,200 institutional investors placed orders, people familiar with the matter have said. 
The company sold $1.1 billion worth of stock to retail investors in the UK and continental Europe, and raised about $3 billion in Japan and around $110 million in Australia, Bloomberg News has reported.
 
The 22 banks on Anthropic’s IPO earned a record $550 million in fees for their work, more than on SpaceX’s IPO. They didn’t receive fees for the so-called over-allotment shares, or for the private placement shares, according to its filings.
 
Demand for SpaceX shares ran to more than $350 billion, with over $100 billion coming from retail, people familiar with the matter said at the time.
 
Anthropic’s listing joins companies linked to AI that have lifted US IPO volume to an all-time high. First time stock sales raised $258 billion this year, beating 2021’s $195 billion haul, excluding financial vehicles such as blank-check firms, data compiled by Bloomberg show. 
 
Anthropic won over investors with a focus on enterprise customers, propelling its run-rate revenue — a measure annualized from a shorter period — to $81 billion as of Oct. 31, up $10 billion from the end of September, its regulatory filings show.
 
Claude Code, the company’s coding agent for software developers, is widely adopted in the industry and has even been used by NASA engineers, the filing shows. Anthropic has more than 11,900 customers delivering $100,000 of revenue each on a trailing 12-month basis as of the end of September, up from about 1,500 in 2025.
 
Anthropic and its rival OpenAI face mounting public scrutiny over AI safety after a string of high-profile hacking incidents by rogue agents, and as the debate rages over whether the technology poses what Anthropic called “existential risks to humanity” in its IPO filing. OpenAI has filed confidentially for a listing but isn’t planning to go public before 2027.

data.title: Cyclone Akvan: Odisha's Mayurbhanj, Balasore under red alert for heavy rain
data.description:
Odisha Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari on Friday said Mayurbhanj and Balasore districts have been placed in the red zone following a reassessment of the weather situation after Cyclonic Storm Akvan made landfall near Gopalpur in Ganjam district.

Pujari said the cyclone had crossed the coast and was moving towards the north and northwest at a wind speed of 55 to 65 kmph, while gradually weakening. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red warning for Mayurbhanj and Balasore, an orange warning for several other districts and a yellow warning for the remaining parts of the state.

"The latest position is that the landfall of the Cyclonic Storm Akvan took place near Gopalpur of the district of Ganjam at around 10:30 to 11:00 a.m., and in the meantime, it has already crossed the coast and is moving towards the north and northwest at a speed of 55 to 65 kmph wind speed, and it is becoming weak," Pujari said.

 

He said the IMD had reassessed the warning levels for different districts.

"As a result, the IMD has reassessed the danger level of different districts, and they have now put Mayurbhanj and Balasore in the Red Zone, and other districts like Keonjhar, Bhadrak, Jajpur, Dhenkanal, Kendrapara, Jagatsinghpur, Nayagarh, Cuttack, Khordha, Puri, Kandhamal, Gajapati, and Ganjam in the Orange Zone, and the rest of the districts of Odisha in the Yellow Zone," he said.

Pujari added that the red zone districts were likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall, while other parts of the state under the yellow warning could also experience rainfall over the next 24 hours.

Meanwhile, Mayurbhanj district has been placed under a red alert, with continuous heavy rainfall making the situation critical, particularly during night hours, Additional District Magistrate Netrananda Mallick said.

Senior district officers are closely monitoring the situation across 12 flood-prone and vulnerable blocks. Cooked food is being distributed to people sheltered at flood relief centres.

Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) teams, along with fire services personnel, remain on high alert and have been deployed at three locations in the district to respond to emergencies. Authorities are monitoring the evolving weather conditions and are prepared to intensify relief and rescue operations if required.

In Bhadrak, Odisha Minister Suryabanshi Suraj said 26,173 people had been relocated, and 145 relief camps had been set up in the district.

"...26,173 people from Bhadrak district have been relocated. 145 relief camps have been set up...Bhadrak received an average of 50.86 mm of rainfall yesterday and only 15.29 mm today. The situation is under control," Suraj said.

data.title: IndusInd Bank invokes clawback provisions against Kathpalia from 2020
data.description:
IndusInd Bank on Friday decided to invoke applicable malus and clawback provisions against its former managing director and chief executive officer (MD & CEO), Sumant Kathpalia, retrospectively from March 24, 2020, the date of his initial appointment as the bank's chief executive. The lender also terminated his employment with immediate effect.
 
The decision was taken by the bank's board, acting as the disciplinary authority, at a meeting on November 20, following the submission of an enquiry report by a former Bombay High Court judge on November 18.
 
The development comes more than 18 months after Kathpalia resigned as MD & CEO on April 29, 2025, taking moral responsibility for accounting discrepancies in the bank's derivatives portfolio.
 
 
While the board had accepted his resignation from the positions of MD & CEO and director, it had communicated that he would continue to remain an employee of the bank until further intimation. Subsequently, disciplinary proceedings were initiated against him under the bank's internal code of conduct. He was placed under suspension with effect from June 18, 2025, pending completion of the proceedings.
 
In its exchange filing on Friday, the bank said the board had decided to terminate his employment with immediate effect and invoke the applicable malus and clawback provisions from the date of his initial appointment as MD & CEO.
 
The decision follows an investigation into discrepancies in the bank's derivatives portfolio, which came to light in March 2025. On March 10, the lender disclosed that an internal review had identified discrepancies that could have an adverse impact of 2.35 per cent on its net worth as of December 2024.
 
The bank subsequently appointed PwC to validate the findings of its internal review and assess the estimated impact. On April 15, it disclosed that PwC had estimated a negative impact of ₹1,979 crore as of June 30, 2024, equivalent to 2.27 per cent of its net worth as of December 2024.
 
The bank had also appointed Grant Thornton to conduct an independent investigation into the root cause of the discrepancies and examine the roles and actions of key employees. According to Grant Thornton's findings, incorrect accounting of internal derivative trades, particularly in cases of early termination, resulted in the recording of notional profits and led to the accounting discrepancies. The cumulative adverse accounting impact on the bank's profit and loss account as of March 31, 2025, was estimated at ₹1,959.98 crore.
 
The bank, in its Q4FY25 earnings, reported a net loss of ₹2,329 crore in the January-March quarter (Q4FY25) — its largest-ever quarterly loss in decades — owing to a substantial jump in provisions and contingencies, weighed down by multiple accounting discrepancies that were discovered in the reporting quarter.
 
The accounting lapses also led to the resignation of Arun Khurana, the bank's deputy chief executive, in April 2025.
 
Kathpalia had headed IndusInd Bank since March 2020, taking over from Romesh Sobti, who led the lender for more than a decade. Before becoming MD & CEO, Kathpalia headed the bank's consumer banking business. He had joined IndusInd Bank in 2008 and previously worked with foreign lenders, including Citibank and Bank of America.

data.title: No further curbs needed on Nvidia chip sales to China: US Treasury secy
data.description:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has said no further restrictions on the sale of older Nvidia chips to China are needed following the Trump administration's move earlier this week to block China's remote access to the latest semiconductors.

The ability of Chinese tech firms to access Nvidia's technology came under scrutiny after CEO Jensen Huang stepped down amid allegations of his affair with an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that uses advanced chips to generate computing power that Chinese firms access remotely.

"The proper chip restrictions are in place," Bessent said in an interview with CNBC on Friday after returning from a trip to Asia with President Donald Trump. "And the remote access has been curtailed." Bessent's comments came a day after the House Foreign Affairs Committee released details of the Commerce Department's approval of the sales of more than 850,000 chips from Nvidia and its competitor AMD to Chinese companies. The Pentagon has identified some of those companies as having ties to the Chinese military.

 

The report tracked applications from Nvidia to sell its H200 chips -- one of its more powerful products, though not the most advanced -- and AMD's applications to sell its roughly comparable MI325X chip to companies that are either located or headquartered in China, or entities with parent companies based in China.

The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security approved the export, re-export, or transfer of 879,868 of these chips to companies with Chinese ties across 21 license applications as of May 11, 2026, the report said. Nvidia and AMD had requested to sell a cumulative total of more than 3.4 million of the chips to Chinese-tied companies across those applications, per the report.

The approvals, which don't necessarily indicate completed sales, included 75,000 for Alibaba, 150,000 for Tencent and its subsidiaries, 43,000 for Baidu, and 4,000 for BYD, according to the report. Each of those companies has been identified by the Defense Department as having ties to the Chinese military.

The report shows the Commerce Department has a "long track record of transparency with Congress about licensing activity for the H200 and equivalent chips, including both approvals and rejections", a spokesperson for the Bureau of Industry and Security said in a statement Friday.

The spokesperson said the Commerce Department's approach to H200 licensing is based on a rule in the Federal Register that was published in January. The rule imposes "significant additional national security-related requirements on license applicants in order to qualify for case-by-case consideration rather than a presumption of denial," the spokesperson said.

An Nvidia spokesperson said in a statement on Friday that the "limited shipments we made under the H200 programme were legal and authorised" by the BIS. "The review and licensing process spanned more than half a year, with approvals subject to strict conditions and limited volumes," the company spokesperson said.

Earlier this week, Nvidia said it was no longer shipping H200 chips to China. The spokesperson said on Friday that shipments had stopped despite prior approvals.

AMD said it complies with US export control laws and regulations and maintains "rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations" in a statement from a spokesperson Friday. "We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity," the spokesperson said.

Chinese technology firms have been bracing for impacts on their ambitious AI development plans as scrutiny mounts on export controls in the US.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has been under intense scrutiny himself in the wake of the turmoil following the Huang affair. Last week, Bessent said he was frustrated with the Commerce Department's delay in placing restrictions on Nvidia chip exports to Megaspeed International, which is under investigation by the US for potentially diverting restricted Nvidia AI chips to China.
